A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ComplexTempQA dataset and study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite changes in placement and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations in Tables 3-7, a human quality study in Section 5 and Figure 3, and dataset analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LLM evaluations, human quality-study results, and appendix dataset analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-D retain the same extraction, template generation, multi-hop construction, unnamed-event disambiguation, and metadata enrichment procedures. The new future-work proposals do not change the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Wikipedia/Wikidata-derived dataset covering 1987-2023 and the same question categories. Newly cited datasets and proposed future extensions are not added to the evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 3-7 retain identical experiment-specific comparator sets and model variants: Llama-chat, Mistral/Mistral-Instruct, Mixtral, GPT-3.5, Falcon, Vicuna, Zephyr, and Wizardlm. The newly discussed temporal-QA approaches are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both specify 12,000 evaluation questions balanced across question types, the same metrics, zero to three shots, and identical DPR context-selection procedures. The human study remains 11 volunteers assessing 450 questions using the same four rating criteria.

E4.justification: The shot and context comparisons, question-type breakdowns, human quality analysis, and Appendix B popularity, category, and country analyses are retained. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting and qualitative study summaries. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The data entries in Tables 1-8 and the empirical figure contents are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports the same zero-shot F1 values of 8.31 for Llama-chat 70B and 7.74 for GPT-3.5; the human-study findings and appendix distributions also match.

T1.justification: The taxonomy, difficulty criteria, and conceptual definitions are retained. Neither version adds or revises mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain the same claims about dataset scale, taxonomy, construction, and LLM evaluation. Calling the taxonomy 'novel' in the revised conclusion reiterates novelty already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Interpretations of question difficulty, few-shot and RAG performance, and English-Wikipedia-related topical and geographic biases remain unchanged. The added future-work sentence proposes extensions and a collective-memory connection without revising an interpretation or limitation of the present study.

D1.justification: The generation details, question templates, metadata schema, experiment prompts, and dataset/code access statement are retained. No new implementation settings, hardware information, or reproducibility instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references covering ChroniclingAmericaQA, Wang et al.'s event-focused temporal QA, Stricker's temporal answer extraction, and two collective-memory studies. A new Section 2 paragraph and the conclusion modestly broaden research positioning while preserving the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and conclusion edits, an added related-work paragraph, a new future-work sentence, and expanded author affiliation/contact text. The section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged and the author block is reformatted. Existing figures, tables, and appendix text are redistributed across pages, including Figure 3 and Tables 3-7. Figure contents and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added discussion of relevant temporal-QA approaches in Section 2 improves research context, while the enlarged Figure 1 makes its reasoning examples easier to read. These are modest gains in context and presentation; the method, empirical support, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
